text: When it is compared with the earlier promise, the apparent difference narrows. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; yet in this scene that very promise is made the matter of a test. The whole action turns upon the single word _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham utters three times. Its meaning alters with each utterance, and each costs him more than the last; he says it first to God, then to Isaac, and at length to the angel.
